name: com.labelixa/zpl
title: Labelixa
description: Thermal label MCP server: render, validate, debug and convert ZPL, EPL, TSPL and CPCL labels.

tools.name: zpl_preview
tools.description: Render ZPL label code and return the label as a PNG image. Use this to SEE what ZPL output looks like — LLMs can write ZPL but cannot otherwise verify the visual result. One call renders one label (use `index` to pick a label from a multi-label stream). The result also carries an 'Open this label in the Labelixa editor' link the user can click to edit, save or share the label.

zpl.description: ZPL source, non-empty, from ^XA to ^XZ. Send real line breaks, not the two characters \n.

tools.name: zpl_validate
tools.description: Pass/fail lint for ZPL — machine-readable diagnostics with line/column, code and severity: unknown commands, missing ^FS, out-of-range parameters, fields outside the label. Fast; run it before zpl_preview whenever you generate or edit ZPL. For a human-readable report with a score, use explain_zpl instead.

dpmm.description: Printer density in dots per mm: 6, 8, 12 or 24 (8 = 203 dpi, 12 = 300 dpi, 24 = 600 dpi). The boundary check measures against it — pass the real value.

width_in.description: Label width in inches. Fields outside it are reported, so a wrong size makes that finding wrong.

height_in.description: Label height in inches. Same as width_in: the boundary check depends on it.

tools.name: zpl_command_help
tools.description: Explain a single ZPL command: syntax, parameters with types/ranges/options, a fragment example and whether the Labelixa renderer draws it. Data comes from the same catalog that powers the public command reference pages.

locale.description: Language for the human-readable fields (name and descriptions). Command codes, syntax strings, examples and parameter names never change.

tools.name: barcode_png
tools.description: Generate a single barcode as a PNG image (Code 128, QR, DataMatrix, EAN-13, UPC-A, PDF417 and more). For a full label with text and layout, write ZPL and use zpl_preview instead.

type.description: Symbology (code128, qr, datamatrix, ean13, upca, pdf417...)

tools.name: language_detect
tools.description: Detect which printer language raw label code is written in (ZPL, EPL, TSPL or CPCL). Heuristic: returns the language plus a confidence TIER (high/medium/low) and signal codes — not a probability.

tools.name: epl_validate
tools.description: Lint EPL/EPL2 label code and return positioned findings with severity as JSON. Checks the command set Labelixa implements from the EPL2 manual — a clean result is not a guarantee that a specific printer accepts the job. Run this before epl_preview; if you are not sure which language the code is, call language_detect first.

tools.name: tspl_validate
tools.description: Lint TSPL/TSPL2 label code and return positioned findings with severity as JSON. Checks the command set Labelixa implements from the TSPL2 manual — a clean result is not a guarantee that a specific printer accepts the job. Run this before tspl_preview; if you are not sure which language the code is, call language_detect first.

tools.name: cpcl_validate
tools.description: Lint CPCL label code and return positioned findings with severity as JSON. Checks the command set Labelixa implements from the CPCL manual — a clean result is not a guarantee that a specific printer accepts the job. Run this before cpcl_preview; if you are not sure which language the code is, call language_detect first.

tools.name: explain_zpl
tools.description: Human-readable health REPORT for a finished ZPL label, with a 0-100 score: sectioned findings (syntax, size/DPI, orientation, barcodes, fonts, graphics memory, job behaviour); sections that cannot be assessed say so and are excluded from the score. Use it to review or explain a label to a person; for a quick pass/fail check while editing, use zpl_validate instead.

dpmm.description: Printer density (8 = 203 dpi). The size/DPI section is scored against it — pass the real value.

width_in.description: Label width in inches; fields outside it are reported.

height_in.description: Label height in inches; same role as width_in.

tools.name: convert_zpl_dpi
tools.description: Rescale ZPL between printer resolutions (203/300/600 DPI): coordinates, fonts, barcode module width and label size are scaled. Embedded ^GF/~DG image data is NOT scaled; the response says so instead of silently passing it through.

source_dpi.description: Resolution the ZPL was written for, in DPI (not dpmm: 203 DPI = 8 dpmm).

target_dpi.description: Resolution to rescale to, in DPI. Equal to source_dpi means no scaling.

tools.name: template_list
tools.description: List Labelixa's first-party label template catalog: id, English name, category, size/density and tags. Read-only product content (no tenant data). Fetch one with template_get; render its ZPL with zpl_preview.

tools.name: template_get
tools.description: Fetch one catalog template: metadata, preview image URL and — for non-premium templates — the ZPL source, ready for zpl_preview. Premium templates return metadata for everyone; their ZPL source requires an API key whose plan includes the premium-template feature (same rule as the website).

template_id.description: Template `id` from template_list (the id, not the display name)

tools.name: save_label
tools.description: Save a ZPL label to a Labelixa account so it can be edited, versioned and printed later. With an API key the label is saved immediately and the saved label id is returned. Without a key the label is held for 24 hours and a one-time link is returned: the user opens it, signs in (free account is enough) and the label lands in their account. Nothing else is stored for anonymous calls.

dpmm.description: Print density in dots per mm: 6, 8, 12 or 24 (8 = 203 dpi)

tools.name: epl_preview
tools.description: Render EPL/EPL2 label code and return a PNG preview. The preview assumes 203 dpi and is an interpretation of the EPL2 manual covering a core command subset — no physical printer validation. `labels` in the response is the TOTAL number of labels the stream prints (a stream may contain several, each ended by `P`); pass `index` to render a different one.

tools.name: tspl_preview
tools.description: Render TSPL/TSPL2 label code and return a PNG preview. The preview assumes 203 dpi and is an interpretation of the TSPL manual covering a core command subset — no physical printer validation. `labels` in the response is the TOTAL number of labels the stream prints (a stream may contain several, each ended by `PRINT`); pass `index` to render a different one.

tools.name: cpcl_preview
tools.description: Render CPCL label code and return a PNG preview. The preview assumes 203 dpi and is an interpretation of the CPCL manual covering a core command subset — no physical printer validation. `labels` in the response is the TOTAL number of labels the stream prints (a stream may contain several, each ended by `PRINT`); pass `index` to render a different one.

tools.name: image_to_zpl
tools.description: Convert an image (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF or SVG, max 200 KB) to a ZPL ^GF graphic command. SVG is rasterised at the chosen density from its declared size (mm/in honoured); SVGs with external references or a DTD are rejected. Returns the ZPL plus measured dimensions and the physical print size at the chosen density. PDF input is REST-only (/v1/graphics).

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image bytes. A data:image/...;base64, prefix and line breaks are accepted.

wrap.description: Wrap the ^GF in a printable ^XA...^XZ label with ^PW/^LL

tools.name: barcode_verify
tools.description: Decode barcodes from a photo or scan of a PRINTED label (PNG, JPEG, BMP or GIF) and report what a software decoder reads back. Honest by design: 'read' does not guarantee every handheld scanner will read it, and 'not read' does not condemn the label (photo angle/focus matter) — the response says so.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image bytes. A data:image/...;base64, prefix and line breaks are accepted.

tools.name: zpl_compatibility
tools.description: Compatibility RISK analysis of ZPL code against a specific printer model, given as manufacturer/model (e.g. 'zebra/zd421'). NOT an emulator and never says 'it works': reports the model's language posture with evidence level and size-rule findings.

model.description: Printer model slug, manufacturer/model, e.g. zebra/zd421

tools.name: bulk_submit
tools.description: Submit a bulk label production job: one ZPL template with {{variable}} placeholders plus data rows (one object per label). Requires an API key whose plan includes bulk jobs. Quota is charged UPFRONT, one operation per row, and failed rows are not refunded; rows per job are capped by plan. Returns the job id — check bulk_status (small jobs usually finish within seconds).

rows.description: One object per label: placeholder name -> value, e.g. [{"name": "Ada", "sku": "A-1"}]

tools.name: bulk_status
tools.description: Status of one bulk job you own: state, attempt count and — when finished — the summary with produced count and per-row failures (row number + reason; failed rows never block the rest). Finished outputs stay downloadable for 7 days via the REST endpoint the response names.

job_id.description: Job id from bulk_submit (32 hex characters; the dashed UUID form is accepted)

tools.name: bulk_list
tools.description: List your recent bulk jobs (id, state, error class, timestamps), newest first. Useful to recover a lost job id; details via bulk_status.

tools.name: printer_language_to_zpl
tools.description: Convert a SATO SBPL, Honeywell (Datamax) DPL or Honeywell (Intermec) IPL label stream to ZPL, so it can be checked with zpl_validate and rendered with zpl_preview. You must name the source language: language_detect does not recognise these three. Real control characters and the manuals' readable notation (<STX>, <ESC>) are both accepted. Commands outside the supported subset (printer settings, RFID, job management, some 2D symbologies) are skipped with a warning, never silently: non-empty `warnings` mean the conversion is not 1:1 and `one_to_one` is false — show the warnings to the user. The output follows each manufacturer's command reference and is not verified on physical printers; check a preview and a test print before production.

code.description: Raw SBPL, DPL or IPL label stream

source_language.description: Language of `code`: sbpl (SATO), dpl (Datamax / Honeywell) or ipl (Intermec / Honeywell)

dpmm.description: Target printer density in dots per mm (8 = 203 dpi)

label_length_mm.description: DPL only: label length in mm. DPL measures rows from the bottom edge, ZPL from the top; without it (or <STX>c in the stream) 6 inches is assumed and a warning is added.

tools.name: printer_list
tools.description: List the printers registered to the Labelixa account (the ones a paired Labelixa DirectPrint agent forwards jobs to). Use a returned device `id` as `device_id` in print_label. Requires an API key whose plan includes printing.

tools.name: print_label
tools.description: Send ZPL to a physical printer through the account's Labelixa DirectPrint agent. Requires an API key whose plan includes printing and a printer from printer_list (or a printer group name). The job is QUEUED, not printed: the response says whether the device is mapped by an agent and when the agent last connected; check print_status for delivery. Always show the user a zpl_preview before printing.

printer_group.description: Printer group name, instead of device_id

idempotency_key.description: Optional key; a retry with the same key returns the first job instead of printing again

tools.name: print_status
tools.description: Status of one print job you own (queued, sent to the agent, delivered or failed) plus when the agent last connected. 'delivered' means the agent handed the bytes to the printer; it does not prove the label came out. `printer_status` is the printer's own status reading taken after delivery (health ready / blocked / unknown, flags such as paused, head_open, media_out, ribbon_out); null means the printer was not asked, and no reading ever confirms that the label printed.
